Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-22 16:30 PT (45m)
Recorded: yes — Fireflies AI
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Marta Ruiz, Derek Lowe, Samir Patel (BrightCart)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna go through a quick hosted chat walkthrough, cover streaming behavior, parameters you should try and retry/fallback patterns — I'm Alex, AE, with Priya on the call who will do the console bits.
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: Hi Alex, thanks. We have about 45 minutes, happy to see the quick flow. Our main thing is low latency for mobile chat and keeping costs reasonable.
[00:20] Derek Lowe: also would like to understand the retry semantics, we've seen double-billing and state issues with other endpoints.
[00:28] Priya Kapoor: yep great, we'll cover idempotency and token accounting. Quick clarifier — BrightCart is planning to use this in customer chat inside merchant dashboards, average convo length around 120 tokens per response, 5 messages context, peak QPS around 30 per region?
[00:42] Samir Patel: that's about right, could spike to 80 for flash sales but sustained is low.
[00:50] Alex Chen: perfect. I'll start with high level then Priya will share the console. First — streaming. Redwood's hosted API supports SSE streaming so you can render tokens as they arrive. One important note is that with streaming we do continuous batching in the backend so short requests can still be aggregated for throughput while keeping first-token latency low.
[01:15] Marta Ruiz: when you say continuous batching, does that mean our single-user flows might wait for batching window?
[01:20] Priya Kapoor: good question — we have a latency SLO for small requests, and the batching window is adaptive based on observed traffic and target SLO. For single-user mobile chat we tune to minimize added latency, usually under 120ms extra beyond model first-token.
[01:36] Derek Lowe: any knob for developers? like prefer-low-latency mode?
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: yes — in the request you can set "prioritize_latency": true (SDK/REST param) or select a runtime profile in the console. That reduces batch window and disables some cross-request fusion optimizations, cost goes up slightly.
[01:55] Alex Chen: moving to params quickly — temperature, top_p and max_tokens. For deterministic assistant replies we recommend temp 0-0.2 and top_p 0.8-1. For more creative responses bump temp. Also show how length impacts cost — each token billed.
[02:12] Samir Patel: do you charge for both prompt and completion?
[02:15] Alex Chen: yes, prompt + completion tokens. We also expose token breakdown in console and via usage API for per-route attribution.
[02:22] Marta Ruiz: and prefix caching — you mentioned earlier that helps reduce cost?
[02:26] Priya Kapoor: correct. If you have repetitive system prompts or user metadata we recommend prefix/KV caching — Redwood caches key/value KV across requests for the same conversation so you only pay for new tokens after the cache hit. In hosted mode the caching is safe and TTL/eviction policies are configurable per app.
[02:45] Derek Lowe: is KV cache the same as like session memory? any PII concerns?
[02:49] Priya Kapoor: it's configurable; you can opt-out of caching for sensitive fields, and we support encryption at rest plus customer-managed keys on Private. For Hosted we offer S3-style retention controls and SOC 2 certs for enterprise customers.
[03:05] Alex Chen: quick demo note — we'll show model pinning in the console and an automatic fallback policy if the preferred model is unavailable due to capacity. Priya?
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: yep I'll share my screen — (screen share starts). Sorry audio clunk — let me walk through the console: route configuration, model pinning, canary rollout.
[03:30] [screen] Priya Kapoor: here is the route, you can attach a rollout policy — perc-based canary or traffic-based. You can also set fallback mappings: e.g., if the 16B family is out, route to a 7B quantized variant. That preserves availability and caps cost.
[03:55] Samir Patel: what's the observed latency delta between the 16B and 7B quantized?
[03:59] Priya Kapoor: on similar hardware, 16B might be 120ms first-token, 7B quantized ~70-80ms, but quality differs. We recommend using Optimize to run evals on your prompts to see regression impact.
[04:16] Derek Lowe: ok, and retries — how do we avoid duplicate side-effects when retrying?
[04:21] Alex Chen: we recommend idempotency keys for non-idempotent operations. For chat generation, if you rely on deterministic finishing you can include an "idempotency_key" header and the system will return cached result for the same key within a short TTL. For streaming partial failures, the client should detect truncated streams (we provide a final event code) and re-request with the same idempotency key.
[04:42] Marta Ruiz: what about cost on retries? if we re-request do we get billed twice?
[04:46] Priya Kapoor: if the retry is served by the idempotency cache you won't be billed twice. If it's a genuine re-exec, billing happens. We expose error codes so you can decide whether to retry automatically or surface to user.
[04:58] [05:00] Alex Chen: quick demo scenario — a mobile client loses connection mid-stream, you could resume with range tokens or re-request. We also support resumable streaming tokens via a session token returned on start in the SDK.
[05:18] Samir Patel: hmm resume is interesting. Is that in hosted now?
[05:21] Priya Kapoor: it's in beta for hosted — SDKs for node/python have helper utilities. We'll include the sample call in the repo.
[05:30] Derek Lowe: regarding monitoring — how do we see per-route cost and latencies?
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: Console shows per-route token breakdown, percentile latencies, and you can export traces to your observability stack. We also have built-in traces that show model selection, kernel path, and cache hit rates.
[05:47] Marta Ruiz: any guardrails for abusive prompts?
[05:50] Alex Chen: yes there's an output safety layer; you can attach post-processing policies and block lists and get safety logs. For enterprise, we can stream logs to your SIEM.
[05:59] [06:05] Priya Kapoor: switching to a short live API demo — I'll use the playground route: sending a chat request with streaming SSE. Code example in Node: (reads) const stream = client.stream.chat(...) — then we show tokens come in. Note transcription sometimes shows chunks joining mid-word.
[06:30] [06:33] (background) Customer: it's a little choppy on their end — chuckle — connection variance.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: that can happen, but the client shows partial token events and the final event with status. If socket closes we recommend client to inspect final status event and re-open with idempotency if needed.
[06:58] Derek Lowe: what about long contexts, say 8k context windows?
[07:02] Alex Chen: supported — we optimize KV caching and offload large prefix tokens via compressed cache. Long context increases memory and cost, we recommend summarization or retrieval-augmented approaches. Redwood Optimize has suggestion rules for when to summarize vs keep full context.
[07:20] Samir Patel: can we set routing by region? we need Europe residency for EU merchants.
[07:24] Priya Kapoor: yes, routing policies support region pins and data residency. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) but hosted can pin to EU regions for data at rest; for audit-heavy customers we support dedicated capacity in EU regions.
[07:44] Marta Ruiz: security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS?
[07:48] Alex Chen: supported — SSO via SAML/OAuth, RBAC roles, audit logs, and KMS integrations. For customer-managed keys we can discuss Private. We'll attach our security whitepaper.
[08:00] [08:05] Priya Kapoor: back to retries — recommended client pattern: exponential backoff with jitter, max 2 retries for user-initiated low-cost requests; for server errors use fallback model route. We show an example pseudocode in the deck.
[08:26] Derek Lowe: can we set per-route max_tokens ceilings to guard runaway costs?
[08:30] Priya Kapoor: absolutely, route config has hard max_tokens and per-message token limits. You can even enforce template checks before sending.
[08:40] Alex Chen: quick note on billing: hosted usage-based; you can also set alerts on spend and a soft cap on QPS. For Dedicated it's reserved commit with predictable unit pricing.
[08:56] Samir Patel: during a flash sale with spikes to 80 QPS, we care about graceful degradation rather than hard errors — what's the typical fallback experience?
[09:05] Priya Kapoor: you can set fallback to a cheaper smaller model or reduce response length via policy; console can auto-apply a degraded route that reduces max_tokens and toggles quantized variants. That keeps request success high while preserving basic UX.
[09:22] Marta Ruiz: show us the rollout policy example?
[09:25] [09:28] Priya Kapoor: (shows JSON snippet) "rollout": {"primary": "m16b-v1", "fallbacks": ["m7b-q4_v1"], "canary": {"percent": 10}} — you can also set circuit-breaker thresholds.
[09:45] Derek Lowe: what metrics do circuit-breakers use?
[09:48] Priya Kapoor: error rate, p95 latency, and backend model queue length. You can tune thresholds in console.
[09:58] Alex Chen: quick troubleshooting note — common failure modes: out-of-memory on bigger models (we provide OOM error codes), slow kernels if seq len unexpected, and network retries. Our docs map error codes to remediation.
[10:16] Samir Patel: curious about streaming partials causing duplicated tokens when retrying — have you seen that?
[10:20] Priya Kapoor: yes, that's why we encourage idempotency keys and final-event checks. If you get a truncated stream and then re-request without idempotency, you'll get a second completion and need to dedupe client-side.
[10:36] [10:40] Marta Ruiz: do you have a sandbox to test under our traffic?
[10:43] Alex Chen: yes — sandbox with throttling and replay of traffic. We can give you API keys and a sandbox project for the POC.
[10:50] Derek Lowe: last thing — latency SLOs: do you publish percentiles?
[10:54] Priya Kapoor: we publish p50/p95/p99 per model in the model catalog and console; for SLAs we offer Dedicated contracts.
[11:05] Alex Chen: ok we'll wrap with next steps — I'll send pricing scenarios and Priya will send the console clip + SDK snippets. Any final Qs?
[11:15] Samir Patel: can you include an example of resumable stream API?
[11:18] Priya Kapoor: yes, adding to action items.
[11:21] Marta Ruiz: great thanks, that was useful.
[11:24] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up.
